status: FIXED BEFORE EXECUTION; amended once after a pre-execution review (before training; the data and smoke stages had run under the first version and smoke is re-run after the amendment) -- see amendment_log

authorization.scope_quoted: UCI official HAR ZIP (one download) + metadata/license; existing torch CPU / TIDES / TeX reused; one TIDES classifier, one model seed, one simple linear control; at most 2 CPU threads, 16 GiB RAM, total wall 3600 s / total process CPU 7200 s for smoke + train/dev/test + bootstrap (installation and PDF builds counted separately); applies to P1-HAR-01 only
authorization.delivered_as: the round-6 instruction document, delivered directly by the user as the execution instruction (2026-10-02)
authorization.not_approved: GPU, paid APIs, new weights, additional libraries, other datasets, additional synthetic seeds

question: On real (distributor-preprocessed) smartphone inertial signals, does a trained official TIDES classifier show the same three effects as on the synthetic task when the SAME held input path is represented on a refined grid: (i) a model-coupling change of the outputs, (ii) a token-mean pooled-readout change that is mostly density weighting, and (iii) a task-risk change (cross-entropy)?
what_this_is: an evaluation that applies an ARTIFICIAL same-held-path refinement to real sensor windows; it is not a validation on naturally irregular acquisitions

data.window: distributor windows of 128 readings at 50 Hz (2.56 s) with 50% overlap between consecutive windows of the same subject; windows are therefore not independent and the analysis unit is the subject
data.calibration_rule: rank the 21 official train subjects by the hex digest sha256('P1-HAR-01:calibration:<id>') in ascending lexicographic order and take the first 4; this rule uses only subject identifiers (no labels, no signals, no performance); the runner re-derives it and refuses to run if the frozen lists differ
data.normalization: per-channel mean and standard deviation over all tokens of the fit-subject windows; applied unchanged to calibration, test and every refined grid (never re-fitted after refinement)
data.labels: 6 classes (1..6 mapped to 0..5); window labels are kept unchanged under every grid condition

representation.convention: the 128 values of a window are 128 HELD intervals of length 1/50 s: value k (k = 1..128) is held on ((k-1)/50, k/50]; t_0 = 0, t_128 = T = 2.56 s; the model state starts at zero at t_0; the horizon is the whole window
representation.note: 128 intervals, not 127 gaps between 128 time stamps; this is the chosen reconstruction of the distributed window, frozen here
representation.step_scale: dt_k / dt_train (1 on the training grid; 1/8 on split sub-intervals), passed as a (B, L) tensor

conditions.S8: every interval split into 8 equal sub-intervals that repeat the held value: 1024 intervals
conditions.H8: the first 64 intervals split into 8, the last 64 unchanged: 512 + 64 = 576 intervals (a same-path density change)

representation.held_values_horizon_labels: unchanged under every condition; repeated values are not new sensor observations
representation.masking: none: every batch has equal lengths, no padding and no mask
representation.resampler: last observation carried forward from the condition's observed (time, value) pairs onto the 128-point training grid; it reads only observed values at or before each grid time (an unobserved prefix is an error, not a fill); on S8 and H8 it reproduces the C0 input exactly (identity control: the maximum absolute input difference is reported, and its logits equal the C0 logits up to float32 rounding, with the maximum absolute logit difference reported); it is not evidence of superiority

model.class: tides.TIDESClassifier (pinned official source, commit 4b51adce2060e7209e002a6a2fd6691a2f6fcc5e; signature read, not guessed)
model.why: the backbone keyword arguments reproduce the P1-REAL-01/02 backbone setting (tides.TIDES with d_hidden 16, ssm_size 16, 1 SSM block, 2 blocks, input-dependent Re Lambda/B/C, exact ZOH, no convolution, no dropout, TIDES defaults otherwise); only d_input (1 -> 9) and the head (per-step linear regression head -> the official mean-pool + Linear(16, 6) classifier head) change. TIDESClassifier's own defaults differ in conj_sym (False), encoder_depth (0) and proj_norm ('rmsnorm'); they are overridden to reuse the existing setting. No other architecture is created.
model.head: official: logits = head(mean_j h_j) with head = nn.Linear(d_hidden, num_classes) (affine), so mean_j head(h_j) = head(mean_j h_j) exactly up to rounding; the pooling-only ablation replaces mean_j by the time-weighted sum sum_j (dt_j/T) h_j at the SAME pooling location and applies the same head; softmax outputs are never averaged
model.pooling_only_status: an inference-time readout ablation, not an official baseline and not a retrained model

training.rng_separation: seed 0 is set in python random, numpy's global RNG (TIDES initialization draws from it) and torch immediately before model construction; the minibatch sampler is random.Random(0), a separate instance; the subject bootstrap uses random.Random(0) inside scssm.real.stats.draws; the smoke run builds and discards its own model with the same seed
training.loss: cross-entropy on the official token-mean logits
training.optimizer: Adam, lr 0.003, batch 32 windows sampled uniformly from fit-subject windows (as in the synthetic runs)
training.calibration: every 100 updates (and at update 0) mean cross-entropy on all calibration-subject windows in eval mode; the state with the lowest calibration cross-entropy is kept (earliest on ties); accuracy is logged but not used for selection; test subjects are never used for selection
training.eval_mode_checks: every module in eval mode during calibration and test; dropout p = 0; batch normalization with running statistics; equal lengths; all step scales > 0; enforced: a failing check is FAIL in training and in evaluation
training.checkpoint: saved once with its sha256 before any test window is read: smoke and train hash and use only the train arrays; eval verifies the checkpoint hash, then reads the test arrays and writes test_opened.json; after that, smoke and train refuse to run (no replacement run)
training.feasible_budget_rule: the smoke run measures s_upd (mean wall seconds per update over updates 3..20; the run must complete all 20 updates, else FAIL), s_cal (mean wall seconds of its two calibration passes, at update 0 and 20) and the per-token inference rate as the larger of s_cal/(N_cal*128) and the rate of one S8 batch of 256 fit windows (L = 1024); projected_train(U) = U*s_upd + (U/100 + 1)*s_cal; projected_eval = 1.5 * rate * (tokens_main + tokens_timing) with tokens_main = N_test*(128+1024+576) + N_test*128 + 3*N_test*128 and tokens_timing = 7*256*sum_cond(2*L_cond + 256); with the ledger total so far (data + smoke) and margins 300 s wall / 600 s CPU (CPU projected with the smoke's cpu/wall ratio), U = 2000 if the wall and CPU sums are within 3600 s / 7200 s; otherwise U = the largest multiple of 100 that satisfies both; if U < 500 the run is INCOMPLETE_BUDGET and test is not opened. The decision is written by the smoke stage and read by the train stage; it is not changed after seeing any performance
training.cap_during_training: the train stage stops and keeps the best-so-far state if its own wall time exceeds its projected allowance plus 300 s; status INCOMPLETE_BUDGET(train) and test is not opened

arms_same_checkpoint.native_mean: official forward on the condition's grid with physical step scales: features from the official backbone, token-mean pooled, affine head (the direct TIDESClassifier forward is compared on C0 for all windows and on the first 256 windows of every condition; maximum absolute differences reported)
arms_same_checkpoint.native_time: the same native features pooled with weights dt_j/T at the same pooling location, then the same affine head (pooling-only ablation)
arms_same_checkpoint.resampled: official forward on the LOCF-resampled training grid (step scale 1); on S8 and H8 the input is identical to C0, so its logits equal the C0 native_mean logits up to float32 rounding (maximum absolute difference reported)
arms_same_checkpoint.check_on_C0: native_mean and native_time coincide on the uniform grid up to rounding; the maximum absolute logit difference is reported

estimands.analysis_unit: subject (windows overlap by 50%; windows, axes and refinements are never counted as independent participants)
estimands.subject_mean_first: every window-level quantity is first averaged within each test subject; overall values are equal-weight means over the 9 test subjects

primary.name: H8 pooled-readout cross-entropy difference
primary.formula: d_s = mean over windows of subject s of [CE(native_mean, H8) - CE(native_time, H8)]; D = (1/9) sum_s d_s (nats)
primary.direction: D > 0 means token-mean pooling has higher cross-entropy than time-weighted pooling of the same features on H8

secondary.risk_change_vs_C0: for arms native_mean, native_time and resampled on S8 and H8: subject means of CE(arm, cond) - CE(native_mean, C0); the resampled arm is an identity control (identical input; its values are float32 rounding noise and are reported as such, not interpreted)
secondary.absolute_CE_and_accuracy: per arm and condition, subject means; accuracy is reported separately from cross-entropy
secondary.prediction_flips: fraction of windows (subject mean) whose argmax under (arm, cond) differs from the argmax under native_mean on C0

output_discrepancy.probability: total variation 0.5 * sum_c |softmax(z) - softmax(z_C0)| (bounded in [0,1]; no denominator)
output_discrepancy.centered_logits: ||ztilde - ztilde_C0||_2 / ||ztilde_C0||_2 with ztilde = z - mean_c z (removes the constant shift that softmax ignores); windows with ||ztilde_C0||_2 < 1e-6 are excluded by this pre-specified rule and their number is reported

secondary.H8_logit_decomposition: per window, on logits (head is affine): p_mean(H8) - p(C0) = W + M with W = sum_j (a_j - w_j) b_j, M = sum_j a_j (z_j - b_j); p_time(H8) - p(C0) = Q = sum_j w_j (z_j - b_j); b_j = C0 token logits of the base interval containing token j, z_j = H8 token logits, a_j = 1/576, w_j = dt_j/T; W equals (7/18)(A - B) per class with A, B the mean C0 token logits over the two halves; reported as subject means of the per-class vectors and of their Euclidean norms; the signed terms are not an additive decomposition of any absolute-value quantity; M_end = the part of M on the 128 interval-end tokens (the model-coupling change evaluated at the base-time states) is a pre-registered split of M; all identities are checked numerically (residuals reported; the pooled arms use head-of-pooled-features, so residuals are at float32 rounding level)
secondary.cost: end-to-end and forward-only wall and process-CPU seconds per condition for one batch of the first 256 test windows (2 warm-up, 5 timed calls, inference mode, 2 threads); timed repeats are not independent samples; the timing block is skipped (recorded as SKIPPED) if running it would exceed the wall cap

estimands.uncertainty: subject-level paired percentile bootstrap: 2000 draws of 9 subjects with replacement (random.Random(0)); the same draws are reused for every quantity; no window-level interval is reported; the 9 d_s values are all shown with their sign count; 9 clusters give only a coarse interval and a degenerate interval is reported as such
estimands.multiplicity: one primary; secondary quantities are descriptive and not corrected; no margin rule is imported from the synthetic runs
estimands.scope: one dataset, one model, one model seed: a conditional result for this checkpoint, not a statement about the population of training runs, about other sensors or about TIDES' benchmarks

control.name: time-weighted moment summary + multinomial linear classifier
control.features: per channel the time-weighted mean sum_j w_j x_j and second moment sum_j w_j x_j^2 (18 features), computed from the grid's (time, value) pairs with w_j = dt_j/T; standardized with fit-subject statistics
control.classifier: nn.Linear(18, 6) trained with full-batch Adam (lr 0.01, 1000 steps, seed 0) on fit-subject windows; no selection, no calibration
control.purpose: a representation-invariance control: its features are identical on C0, S8 and H8 up to rounding (the maximum absolute difference and the CE difference are reported); it is NOT a task ceiling, SOTA or capacity-matched baseline

stored_outputs.in_git: results/raw/P1-HAR-01/: acquisition.json, data_hash.json, smoke.json, train.json, train.log, checkpoint.pt (about 30 KB) + sha256, eval.jsonl (per-window: subject, label, pooled logits of every arm and condition, CE, prediction, distances, H8 decomposition vectors), C0_token_logits.f16.npy.gz (2947 x 128 x 6, float16), eval_summary.json, control.json, aggregate.json, cost_ledger.json; pooled logits are stored in float64; the in-git outputs of eval (eval.jsonl + C0 token logits) must stay under size_cap_mb_in_git
stored_outputs.local_only: data/har/derived/: cached arrays and S8/H8 per-token logits (float16); regenerable from the checkpoint
stored_outputs.why: pooled logits and the decomposition terms allow every reported statistic to be recomputed without a forward pass

budget.ledger: results/raw/P1-HAR-01/cost_ledger.json (every stage, including data parsing, smoke, refused/failed attempts and bootstrap; wall and process CPU separately); a stage refuses to start when the cumulative total plus its projected cost would exceed either cap
budget.excluded_from_this_budget: the data download (32.97 s), extraction, PDF builds and package builds (recorded elsewhere)
budget.smoke_note: the smoke training loop is capped at 45 s so that the whole stage (model build, two calibration passes, one S8 probe batch) stays near 60 s; the stage wall is what the ledger records

stop_conditions.INCOMPLETE_BUDGET: feasible updates < 500, or training exceeds its allowance: the checkpoint is kept, test is not opened, the status is reported
stop_conditions.FAIL: non-finite loss or an eval-mode check failing: reported as FAIL, no replacement run
stop_conditions.no_changes_after_test: no change of seed, loss, estimand, head, dataset, H8 strength or budget after any test window is read; enforced by test_opened.json and the config sha256 recorded in train.json
